methodologyNotes: Call-tracking / call-analytics software (CallRail / WhatConverts / CallTrackingMetrics class). Pricing figures were collected from each vendor's public pricing page on the accessedAt date recorded per source; where a second independent source (vendor pricing-guide, comparison roundup, or G2/Capterra listing) confirms the same figure it is attached as 'corroboration', satisfying the two-source rule. Each capture carries its OWN accessedAt: re-reading a vendor's page refreshes the source date alone, so a corroboration is usually dated earlier than the source beside it, and it evidences the figure as of the day we read that second page rather than as of the source read. /changes/ applies that directly — a corroboration read before a price move is not counted as a witness to it. No figure is ever invented. This category bills as subscription + metered usage: most vendors charge a flat monthly base PLUS per-minute (local/toll-free), per-number, recording, and transcription fees on top, while a sub-segment (Nimbata, Infinity) bills per ANSWERED CALL instead of per minute. Plans are normalized to the dataset shape: monthlyUsd is the recurring base, minutesIncluded/callsIncluded carry bundled quota where the vendor publishes one (usually null — these platforms meter usage rather than bundle it; the entry tier's headline allowance is recorded where stated, e.g. CallRail's 250 local minutes / 5 numbers), overagePerMin is the marginal local per-minute rate and overagePerCall the per-answered-call rate. Toll-free per-minute, recording, transcription, SMS and per-number rates are preserved in plan notes rather than dropped. IMPORTANT FABRICATION-GUARD NOTE: some vendors (WhatConverts, CallTrackingMetrics) publish a SINGLE platform-wide per-minute overage that applies identically to every tier rather than a per-plan rate; to avoid presenting a falsely uniform column, that single rate is recorded once on the relevant tier(s) with the caveat in notes, not copied across all plans. WildJar and Convirza were named here until 2026-09-08 and do NOT belong: a first-party re-read that day found both metering per tier rather than platform-wide. Convirza charges $0.08/min on Starter and $0.05 on Agency, which is what its rows record. WildJar publishes $0.10/min on Agency and no per-minute rate at all on Starter, whose $150 base buys 500 bundled minutes instead — the $0.05 and $0.04 this note carried until that day came from a pricing page WildJar has abandoned. CallRail was listed here until 2026-09-08 and is NOT one of them: its per-minute rate is set by the bundled allotment, not by the platform (local minutes $0.06 at the 250-minute entry allotment, stepping down to $0.045 at 4,000 minutes), so its overagePerMin records the entry allotment's rate and its notes say which allotment that is. Quote-only / sales-gated vendors (Invoca, Phonexa, Marchex, CallSource, Retreaver) carry empty plans[] with a provenance note stating where pricing was sought and why no figure was recorded — never a guessed number. Per-minute developer-style metering means the cost normalizer must combine base + (minutes x rate). HIPAA/BAA and integration fields reflect what each vendor states publicly; null means not published, not absence. This is a static snapshot intended to be refreshed from our scheduled public-page monitoring pipeline.

Month-to-month price; $95/mo billed annually, which is the figure callrail.com/pricing shows before you touch its toggle.

vendors.provenance: Four-tier 2026 plan structure read from callrail.com/pricing rendered in a headless browser on 2026-09-08 (the page is JavaScript-rendered; a plain fetch returns no prices). The page opens on its Yearly toggle — CallRail's own code defaults the billing period to annual — so the figures it shows first are the ANNUAL-BILLED ones: Lead Tracking $50 / Lead Tracking Complete $95 / Lead Conversion $150 / Lead Conversion Complete $195 per month. Switching to Monthly gives $55 / $105 / $165 / $215, and CallRail's own "See all Lead Tracking plans" table labels the two columns "Yearly" and "Monthly" in those words. The monthly price recorded holds the MONTH-TO-MONTH figure, as it does across this dataset, with the annual discount carrying the annual saving; records before 2026-09-08 held the annual-billed figure in the monthly price recorded and then applied a further ~10% discount on top of it, understating the month-to-month price by about 10% and counting the annual saving twice. Corrected 2026-09-08 and logged in data/corrections.jsonl. Metered usage is billed on top and is set by the bundled allotment, not platform-wide: at the 250-minute entry allotment local minutes are $0.06, toll-free $0.08, SMS $0.03; the same table meters local minutes at $0.045 on the 4,000-minute allotment, which is the rate this record previously carried on the entry tier. The market leader (700+ integrations). HIPAA/BAA available for healthcare accounts. The corroboration recorded here on 2026-06-11 (toolcomparelab, "From $50/mo") corroborated the annual-billed figure rather than the month-to-month one now recorded, and that host has since gone offline (503, with no archive.org capture of it), so it was removed rather than left standing beside a figure it does not support.

vendors.provenance: Tiered base read from nimbata.com/pricing rendered in a headless browser on 2026-09-08. The page carries a billing toggle that LOADS IN THE ANNUAL STATE and is easy to miss — a zero-width, transparent checkbox whose two labels are drawn in CSS pseudo-elements — so the figures a visitor sees first are the annual-billed ones: Pro $35 / Marketing $80 / Agency $120 per month, each printed beside a struck-through month-to-month price. Switching the toggle to Monthly gives Pro $39 / Marketing $89 / Agency $149, and the page's own pricing script sets the same three pairs. The monthly price recorded here is the MONTH-TO-MONTH figure, as it is across this dataset; the Marketing and Agency rows held the annual-billed figure until 2026-09-08, while the Pro row had already been re-based, so one field meant two different things inside one vendor. Corrected 2026-09-08 and logged in data/corrections.jsonl. The annual discount carried 20 on all three rows — the page's "Save up to 20% with an annual plan" headline, which is a ceiling only Agency approaches; each row now records its own saving (10% Pro, 10% Marketing, 19% Agency). Distinctive model: one flat charge per ANSWERED call, not per minute. That per-call rate IS carried in the page's own rate table, but the table fills in only after a country lookup that failed on our read, so every cell rendered as a dash; the per-call overage rate stays blank rather than take a figure the page did not display, and the rate is country-dependent and published as "starting at" in any case. A vendor that publishes a BAA commitment on a marketing page and disclaims HIPAA in the contract that governs the account has not established either field, so both stay blank rather than resolve a contradiction in the vendor's favour. vendors.provenance: US tiers read from wildjar.com/pricing in a headless browser on 2026-09-08, and confirmed by a second independent read. THIS RECORD WAS REBUILT THAT DAY, because the page it had been citing is no longer WildJar's pricing page. It had held Starter $39, Agency $89 and Mammoth $159 from wildjar.com/pricing-united-states — a page nothing on the site links to any more, whose footer still reads 2024, whose testimonials are placeholder Lorem Ipsum, and whose sitemap entry was last touched 2026-05-24 against 2026-09-04 for the live page. It still answers with HTTP 200 and still serves the old figures, which is exactly why the error survived re-verification: a scanner pointed at that URL keeps confirming prices WildJar no longer charges. The live page publishes, for the United States, Starter at $150/mo — a different product, bundling 4 tracking numbers, 500 minutes and AI transcription rather than metering from zero — Growth/Agency at $89/mo plus usage, and Mammoth with no price at all ("Talk to the pack", every comparison cell reading Custom), so Mammoth is no longer carried as a priced tier. Metered rates are $8.50/mo per local number, $0.10/min on calls, $0.06 per SMS and $0.04/min for AI transcription. There is NO annual billing: the words annual, yearly and per year appear zero times, and the FAQ states monthly subscriptions only, no setup fees, no lock-in, billed in arrears with 30 days notice. Two cautions for whoever reads this page next. It is one page for four regions (Australia, New Zealand, United Kingdom, United States) held as hidden blocks with AUSTRALIA ACTIVE ON LOAD, switched by a script that only shows and hides — so a fetch or a scan reads Australian dollars unless the United States control is clicked. And every US numeral except the AI Voice Agent charge is identical to the Australian one, while New Zealand and the United Kingdom are genuinely localised; whether that is deliberate parity or an un-localised block cannot be settled from the page, and it is recorded here rather than smoothed over. The G2 listing that corroborated the old Starter price was removed with that price; it still stands on Agency, which G2 recorded at the same $89 the live page publishes today. HIPAA/BAA not published.

vendors.provenance: UK-headquartered marketing-attribution / call-analytics vendor, re-read in a headless browser on 2026-09-08. THIS RECORD WAS REBUILT THAT DAY. It previously held a single plan called "Per-user (entry)" at $50/user/mo, described as a vendor-stated USD equivalent, with a 20% annual discount. None of that is on the page: mediahawk.co.uk/pricing publishes two priced tiers, Starter and Professional, at £199/mo and £299/mo month-to-month (£179 and £269 on an annual contract), plus an Enterprise tier quoted on application. Both priced tiers state "Unlimited users" and the phrase "per user" does not appear anywhere on the page, so the per-user model was never real; the page contains no "$" character at all, so nothing on it was ever a vendor-stated USD figure; and the annual saving is stated as 10% in three places and computes to 10.05% and 10.03%, not 20%. The annual discount applies to the fixed subscription only — per-minute and per-call charges are not discounted. Nothing is bundled: included minutes and included calls are not recorded because metering starts at the first minute, and each tier includes either 1 dynamic number pool or 10 static numbers. Metered charges are published in pence and vary two ways: the per-call connection fee by tier (15p Starter, 12p Professional, to landline or mobile) and the per-minute rate by number type and destination (2.5p-14p; local presence and 03 numbers 2.5p to landline and 9.5p to mobile). Onboarding is free and explicitly stated as included in every plan. Every money field in this dataset is denominated in USD, and this vendor publishes no USD price, so every one of them is left blank rather than converted at a rate the vendor does not quote — the previous $50 was exactly such a figure and it matched nothing. The pricing page also loads with its billing toggle already on Annually, behind a zero-size transparent checkbox whose two state words are unclickable, with the month-to-month price struck through; a future re-read that trusts the first figures rendered would record £179 and £269, which are the annual prices.
